parole.testo: From Middle Persian 𐫀𐫤𐫍𐫢 (ʾthš /⁠ātaxš⁠/, “fire”), borrowed from Avestan 𐬁𐬙𐬀𐬭𐬱 (ātarš, “fire”) for its special meaning in Zoroastrianism and well preserved unlike the other word آذر (âzar, “fire”). Doublet of آذر. Ultimately from Proto-Iranian *HáHtr̥š; see there for further information.

parole.significato: Arzah, the eastern division of the seven realms
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian ’lz’ (Arzah), from Avestan 𐬀𐬭𐬉𐬰𐬀𐬵𐬍 (Arəzahī, “east”). The term initially was identified with the Indus region, with the expansion of knowledge during the Middle Iranian era, it came to be applied to most of South Asia.
From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾlgnd /⁠arγand⁠/), from Avestan 𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬖𐬀𐬧𐬙 (ər^əγaṇt, “tumultuous, uproarious, raging”).

parole.significato: the demon of death in the Avesta
parole.testo: From Middle Persian ʾstwhʾt' (astwihād), from Avestan 𐬀𐬯𐬙𐬋.𐬬𐬌𐬜𐬁𐬙𐬎 (astō.viδātu, “who breaks a bone”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ésth₁ (bone) (more at استخوان) and Proto-Indo-European *weh₁y- (twist).
From Middle Persian 𐭧𐭭𐭰𐭬𐭭 (hanjaman, “congregation, assembly, community”), from Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬧𐬘𐬀𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬀 (haṇjamana, “assembly”).

parole.significato: Apaosha; the personification of drought and the principle enemy of the yazata of rain, Tishtrya
parole.testo: From Middle Persian ʾpwš (apōš), from Avestan 𐬀𐬞𐬀𐬋𐬱𐬀 (apaōša), derived from Proto-Iranian *apauša (“unthriving”). Inherited from Middle Persian ʾylmʾn' (ērmān), derived from Avestan 𐬀𐬌𐬭𐬌𐬌𐬇𐬨𐬁 (aⁱriiə̄mā, “fellow tribesman; name of a divinity”), from Proto-Iranian *aryamā́, ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *aryamā́ (“fellow, companion; member of one's own tribe/clan; name of a deity”).

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾp̄ʾhtl /⁠abāxtar⁠/, “north”), derived from Avestan 𐬀𐬞𐬁𐬑𐬙𐬀𐬭𐬀 (apāxtara, “north; direction of the daevas, direction of Ahriman, direction of Hell”), from Old Iranian *apāxtara (“retrograde, backward-turning”), comparative stem based on *apāk-/*apāŋ

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾpwlnʾd /⁠aburnāy⁠/, “underage, youth”), a Zoroastrian legal term borrowed from Avestan 𐬀𐬞𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬁𐬌𐬌𐬎 (apər^ənāiiu, “underage”), the negative of 𐬞𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬁𐬌𐬌𐬎 (pər^ənāiiu, “adult”), from Proto-Iranian *pr̥Hnáh (“full, filled”).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (wyš /⁠wēš⁠/, “more”), probably borrowed from Avestan 𐬠𐬌𐬱 (biš, “twice”), from 𐬛𐬀𐬌𐬠𐬌𐬙𐬌𐬌𐬀 (daⁱbitiia).
From بیـ (bē /bi, “-less, without”) + هوده (hūda /hude, “benefit, use”, from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (hwdʾk' /⁠hudāg⁠/), borrowed from Avestan 𐬵𐬎𐬜𐬃𐬢𐬵 (huδā̊ŋh)).

Inherited from Middle Persian twlkʾ (/⁠tōlag⁠/, “baby animal, whelp”), from Avestan 𐬙𐬀𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬥𐬀 (taᵘruna, “young”), Northern Luri تیله (tilə). Cognate with Sanskrit तरुण (taruṇa, “juvenile”). Cf. تور (tōr /tur, “uncivilized”).
From Middle Persian [script needed] (xwarrah, “divine glory, splendour”), a borrowing from Avestan 𐬓𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬀𐬵 (xᵛar^ənah). Doublet of فر (farr), which was inherited.

Learned borrowing from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (hwytw(k)ds /⁠xwēdōdah⁠/), from Avestan 𐬓𐬀𐬉𐬙𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬛𐬀𐬚𐬀 (xᵛaētuuadaθa). Earlier Persian Rivayats do not use this spelling, but rather a variety of forms such as خیتُودَث (xētūdas), خْویدْیُودَث (xwēdyūdas), خْویتُودَث (xwētūdas), etc.

parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (dhmk' /⁠daxmag⁠/), borrowed from Avestan 𐬛𐬀𐬑𐬨𐬀 (daxma), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰm̥bʰ- (“to dig”). Compare Old Armenian դամբան (damban, “tomb”), Ancient Greek τᾰ́φος (tắphos, “tomb”). Attested in New Persian since the Shāhnāma, 1010.

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (druwand /⁠dlwnd⁠/, “sinful, unrighteous [one]”), borrowed from Avestan 𐬛𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬧𐬙 (druuaṇt), 𐬛𐬭𐬆𐬔𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬧𐬙 (drəguuaṇt), from Proto-Iranian *dráwgah-wánts (“follower of the Lie”). Compare Sanskrit द्रुह्वन् (druhvan).
Inherited from Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠duwēst⁠/), from Avestan 𐬛𐬎𐬎𐬈𐬯𐬀𐬙𐬈 (duuesate). Cognate with Sogdian [script needed] (dwyst). Displaced by دوصد (do-sad) in eastern dialects of Persian.

Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (lyšk' /⁠rēšag⁠/), borrowed from Avestan 𐬭𐬀𐬉𐬱𐬀 (raēša), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *wréh₂ds (“root”). Cognate with Baluchi ریشَگ (rīšag, “root”)

Inherited from Middle Persian 𐭦𐭱𐭲 (zyšt' /⁠zišt⁠/, “hateful, ugly”), a loanword from Avestan 𐬰𐬀𐬉𐬱𐬀 (zaēša) from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰáyždas, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéysd-os, from *ǵʰeysd- (“anger, agitation”). Cognate with Proto-Germanic *gaistaz (“ghost, mind”).

Inherited from Middle Persian znd (zand, “understanding, explanation, commentary”), from Avestan 𐬰𐬀𐬌𐬥𐬙𐬌 (zainti, “understanding”), from Avestan verbal root Avestan 𐬰𐬀𐬥- (zan-, “to know, to understand”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵneh₃-ti-. Cognate with Ancient Greek γνῶσις (gnôsis).
From Middle Persian swkšydns (sōšyans), from Avestan 𐬯𐬀𐬊𐬳𐬌𐬌𐬀𐬧𐬝 (saoš́iiaṇt̰).

From Middle Persian swknd (sōgand, “oath”), from Avestan [Term?] (/⁠saokanta⁠/, “sulphur”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱewk- (“white”). Related to سوختن (sōxtan, “to burn”), and سوگ (sōg, “sadness, mourning”).

parole.significato: Frashokereti, the final renovation of the world, wherein evil is destroyed, and the world is purified
parole.testo: From Middle Persian [script needed] (prš(y)gyrd /⁠fraš(a)gird⁠/, “Frashokereti; making wonderful, excellent”), from Avestan 𐬟𐬭𐬀𐬱𐬋𐬐𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬙𐬌 (frašōkər^əti).

From Middle Persian 𐫖𐫏𐫗𐫇𐫃 (mynwg /⁠mēnōg⁠/, “the spiritual world, the intangible world”), borrowed from Avestan 𐬨𐬀𐬌𐬥𐬌𐬌𐬎 (maⁱniiu, “spirit”). Inherited from Middle Persian [Term?], from Avestan [Term?]. Compare with Northern Kurdish pênsed. Displaced by پنجصد (panj-sad) in eastern dialects of Persian.

parole.significato: the highest realm of Heaven; the realm of infinite light
parole.testo: From Middle Persian grdmʾn (garōdmān, “heaven”), from Avestan 𐬔𐬀𐬭𐬋.𐬛𐬆𐬨𐬁𐬥𐬀- (garō.dəmāna-, “house of song; Paradise”). parole.significato: yasht (any of a collection of hymns and prayers)
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian yšt' (yašt, “prayer, worship”), probably from Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬱𐬙𐬀 (yašta, “honored”).

parole.significato: to worship, to perform Zoroastrian rituals
parole.testo: Inherited from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (yštn' /⁠yaštan⁠/), borrowed from Avestan 𐬫𐬀𐬰𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (yazaⁱti, “to worship, to venerate”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hyáȷ́ati, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁yaǵ-.
